setlist_extra.title: Maybe You Know How I Feel

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Looks Like Rain** (2 reviews): Features a far-out Jerry solo; Reviewer's favorite, with an incredible break [16][24]
- **Eyes Of The World** (2 reviews): Played fast, yet Jerry contributes beautiful licks; Somewhat fast, but Jerry shreds it [16][19]
- **Touch Of Grey** (1 review): A very funky version, one of the few good ones the reviewer has heard [22]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): China Cat into Rider is played at high speed [22]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Double chorus occurs during the break [24]
- **Throwing Stones** (1 review): Has a great jam [16]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Throwing Stones into Morning Dew is the only such pairing the reviewer can find, making the show unique [21]

## Setlist highlights

- **Maybe You Know**: rare: 6 archived performances [26]

## The recordings

- **gd83-04-20.sbd.miller.27860.sbeok.flacf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 155 min; rated 3.94/5 by 17 [1]. Said about its sound: Matrix is a sweet upgrade over the original source; Occasional zaps heard are from the PA system, not the recording; Phil comes through nicely; Miller transfer has Phil loud and clear throughout [19][20][25]
- **gd1983-04-20.aud.wise.92322.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 21 songs; 156 min; rated 4.6/5 by 5 [2]
- **gd83-04-20.sennheiser.dodd.10090.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 21 songs; 157 min; rated 3.33/5 by 5 [7]. Said about its sound: First set was taped with Beyer microphones, second set with Sennheiser 421s; Reviewer says levels on this audience recording are too low and the first set is weak [14][17]
- **gd1983-04-20.139277.set1.fob.beyer.m160.miller.flac16**: source not stated; 11 songs; 66 min [12]. Said about its sound: Uploader says the master cassette has been played heavily and sounds worn [12]

## Around the show

- Attendee recalls a rowdy crowd after tailgating from mid-afternoon [15]
- First set had sound trouble, but attendee counts it among favorite shows seen; Bob's vocals strong all night [24]
- PA problems occurred throughout the show [12]
- Reviewer finds the first set epic and the second set only fair [14]
- Show contains elements of all the solid shows of spring 1983 [15]
- Morning Dew is good but fast; reviewer points to 06-18-1983 for a better Dew from this era [19]
- Reviewer rates it very fast-paced, with Jerry and Phil tight, judged against other 1983 shows [21]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd83-04-20.sbd.miller.27860.sbeok.flacf**: source: SBD> Master Cassette> Reel> Dat (SV3800/48k), plus patch from FOB Sennheiser 421> Master Cassette; [1]. Also: Soundboard to master cassette to reel to DAT, with a front-of-board Sennheiser 421 patch; transferred and edited by Charlie Miller [1]
- **gd1983-04-20.aud.wise.92322.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Unknown; source: Sennheiser MD-421's > Sony TC-D5, recorded from "upper level". [2]. Also: Audience-source patch from ShnID 10090 covers a tape flip in Drums [2]
- **gd83-04-20.sennheiser.dodd.10090.sbeok.shnf**: source: FOB-Senn. 421Âs>Sony D-5>CM>DAT>CDR [7]. Also: Listener got a copy two days after the show; recalls Charlie Miller's labeled master was in hand when copied in 1983 [14]
- **gd1983-04-20.139277.set1.fob.beyer.m160.miller.flac16**: taped by Charlie Miller; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Beyer M160 > Sony TC-D5M > Cassette Master (Sony WM-D6C/Maxell UDXL-II) [12]. Also: Set 1 from Beyer M160 front-of-board; Sennheiser 421 patch used for set 2 and encore [12]
